0031 — Layered architecture and the allowed-imports table

Status: proposed; accepted when the maintainer merges the pull request for #2087.

Problem

src/ holds about 400 TypeScript files. AGENTS.md names six layers, and tools/check-architecture.ts enforces five narrow rules between them. Most of the tree sits outside any named layer: many top-level modules (config.ts, baseline.ts, plan.ts, fix/, sbom/, and others) have no declared place, so nothing stops a new module from reaching across a boundary. Four import cycles are baselined, and src/engine.ts and src/source-usage.ts import node:fs directly. The follow-up issues of epic #1990 (cycles #2090, pure core #2091, detector contract #2092, adapters #2093, errors #2094, reporters #2114, fitness tests #2115) each need one agreed target to move toward.

This record fixes that target. It moves no code and changes no behavior.

Decision

Offing is one package with seven layers. A module belongs to exactly one layer. A layer may import only the layers listed for it below, plus the node: built-ins and packages listed for it. Imports between modules of the same layer are allowed unless a later record narrows them.

Layers

Layer Lives in Owns
1. Domain src/domain.ts, src/errors.ts, src/purl.ts, src/vers/, src/paths.ts Types, output contracts, pure helpers with no I/O
2. Detector SDK src/sdk.ts The public seam: API version, stable ID, one scan operation
3. Core src/engine.ts, src/source-usage.ts, src/source-files.ts, src/usage/, src/registry.ts, src/scan-cache.ts, src/detector-inputs.ts, src/file-system.ts Detector attribution, sorting, repository traversal, usage matching, rule loading
4. Detectors src/detectors/ Reading manifests and lockfiles for one ecosystem
5. Services analysis built on a scan result: src/plan*.ts, src/migration-*.ts, src/fix/, src/sbom/, src/drift/, src/export/, src/inventory/, src/baseline.ts, src/diff.ts, src/forecast*.ts, src/receipt*.ts, src/agent-tools.ts, and similar Migration context, plans, baselines, exports. No argument parsing, no host protocol
6. Reporters src/reporters.ts, src/reporters/, src/mermaid.ts Turning results into text, JSON, SARIF, HTML, and other formats
7. Adapters src/cli.ts, src/cli-main.ts, src/commands/, src/mcp*.ts, src/lsp.ts, src/action*.ts, src/github-action.ts, src/tui.ts, skills/, plugins/ Translating one host interface to services and reporters

Registry data (registry/*.json) is data, not a layer. It holds no logic, and only the core loads it.

Allowed imports

Read a row as "the layer in the first column may import the layers marked ✓".

Importer \ Imported Domain SDK Core Detectors Services Reporters Adapters
1. Domain ✓
2. Detector SDK ✓ ✓
3. Core ✓ ✓ ✓
4. Detectors ✓ ✓ source-usage and usage/ only ✓
5. Services ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
6. Reporters ✓ ✓ (types and helpers only) ✓
7. Adapters ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ (through scan-builtins.ts only) ✓ ✓ ✓

Notes on the table:

  • Core never imports detectors. Built-in detectors reach the engine only through src/scan-builtins.ts, which an adapter or service calls. This is the existing engine-no-detectors rule.
  • Detectors may use the shared usage matcher (source-usage.ts, usage/) because it is the shared pass they declare patterns for. They may not import services, reporters, or adapters.
  • Reporters sit below adapters and render services' output. A reporter does not run a scan.
  • Nothing imports an adapter except another adapter. An adapter file that other layers need to import is a sign that logic belongs in a service.
  • The SDK depends only on the domain layer, except that it re-exports analyzeSourceUsage from source-usage.ts today. #2092 removes that exception by exposing detectors' usage access through the detector contract instead.

Runtime access rules

Rule Applies to
No node:fs, node:fs/promises, node:child_process, node:http, node:https, node:net, node:tls, node:dgram, node:dns, or global fetch Domain, SDK, and core. Since #2091 they reach files through the ScanFileSystem interface (src/file-system.ts); src/node-file-system.ts and src/bundled-assets.ts are the Node implementations, outside the core
No network modules or fetch Detectors and reporters. This is the scan-offline guarantee.
Network use is allowed only in the named update and publishing modules that exist today (data-update.ts, pr-comment.ts, action-fix-pr.ts, action-tracking-issue.ts, commands/data.ts) Services and adapters; never reachable from a scan
No eval, new Function, vm, or dynamic import() of repository paths Every layer. Repository contents are parsed, never executed.

How the checker adopts this

The decision does not change the checker. Each follow-up lands its own rule in tools/check-architecture.ts with the code move that makes it true, so the check never fails on code that has not moved yet:

  1. #2090 empties tools/architecture-baseline.json, so a new cycle fails with no exception list.
  2. #2091 adds the no-node:fs/no-network rule for domain, SDK, and core.
  3. #2092 gives detectors one typed contract and removes the SDK's import of source-usage.ts.
  4. #2093 moves logic out of adapters and adds "nothing imports an adapter except an adapter".
  5. #2114 gives reporters one interface and adds the reporters row.
  6. #2115 turns this table into fitness tests with a clear message per rule.

Alternatives considered

  • Separate workspace packages per layer. Rejected for now, for the reason already in ARCHITECTURE.md: interface and implementation share one release lifecycle, and a package boundary would add publishing work without adding a check that an import rule does not already give.
  • Keep only the five existing rules. Rejected: most modules have no declared layer, so the checker cannot say whether a new import is wrong.
  • Forbid same-layer imports. Rejected as too strict for services, where plan.ts legitimately builds on plan-build.ts and plan-waves.ts. Cycles are forbidden separately by #2090.

Consequences

  • Every module has one layer, and a reviewer can answer "may this import that?" from one table.
  • The AGENTS.md table stays the short summary and links here for the full rules.
  • Layers 5 and 7 are described by file patterns because the modules are still flat in src/. Moving them into directories is optional and not required by this decision.
  • Until the follow-ups land, the checker enforces less than this record states. The record is the target; the checker is the floor.

Review

Revisit after #2115 lands, when every row has a test, or when a module cannot be placed in one layer.
